findings.problem: status: String allows any arbitrary string value (e.g. "deleted", "sent", "pendingX") instead of a closed set of valid packet states.
findings.failure_mode: Domain invariant for packet lifecycle cannot be enforced at compile time; any string is accepted as a valid status, making illegal states representable.
findings.fix: Replace status: String with a domain enum: enum PacketStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent }.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool is a primitive lifecycle flag that can be inconsistent with status (e.g. status="sent" but is_validated=false).
findings.failure_mode: Redundant boolean flags with the status string create state-space explosion; a packet can reach "sent" without being validated, bypassing domain invariants.
findings.fix: Remove is_validated boolean. Encode validation state inside the PacketStatus enum or use a typestate pattern (Pending -> Validated -> Sent) so transitions are type-enforced.

findings.problem: is_sent: bool is a primitive lifecycle flag that is redundant with status and can conflict (e.g. status="sent" but is_sent=false).
findings.failure_mode: Boolean flag and status string can diverge, making it impossible to determine the true lifecycle state at runtime. This defeats both the status and boolean as reliable indicators.
findings.fix: Remove is_sent boolean. Let the PacketStatus enum (or typestate) carry the sent state directly.

findings.problem: PacketWorkflow struct allows construction of any field combination with no typestate. mark_sent does not enforce that a packet was validated before being marked sent.
findings.failure_mode: An unvalidated packet (is_validated=false) can transition directly to sent state, violating the intended domain invariant that validation precedes sending.
findings.fix: Use typestates: struct Pending { id: PacketId, is_validated: bool }; struct Validated { id: PacketId }; struct Sent { id: PacketId, sent_at: TimestampMs }. mark_sent takes Validated and returns Sent, making illegal transitions uncompileable.

findings.problem: mark_sent returns PacketWorkflow directly instead of Result<PacketWorkflow, PacketError>. There is no error taxonomy for why marking might fail.
findings.failure_mode: callers cannot distinguish success from failure; if validation or other preconditions are violated in the future, the function has no way to communicate the error.
findings.fix: Return Result<PacketWorkflow, PacketSendError> where PacketSendError is a domain enum (e.g. PacketSendError::NotValidated, PacketSendError::AlreadySent). Require a validated input type to make preconditions type-enforced.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive instead of a domain newtype (e.g. PacketId). sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is a raw primitive timestamp.
findings.failure_mode: Raw primitives allow passing arbitrary strings as packet IDs and raw u64 values as timestamps, enabling confusion between domain concepts at compile time.
findings.fix: Introduce: pub struct PacketId(String); // or bytes/newtype with boundary parsing. pub struct TimestampMs(u64); Parse and validate at I/O boundaries into these types.

findings.problem: item.status = "sent".to_string() allocates a new String on every call. Combined with id: String, every PacketWorkflow carries heap allocations.
findings.failure_mode: Repeated allocation of status string on every mark_sent call creates unnecessary heap pressure and prevents zero-copy patterns in hot paths.
findings.fix: Replace String fields with enum-based status (no allocation). For id, consider &str at function boundaries or use a compact newtype. If String is unavoidable, use try_reserve for any Vec growth.

findings.problem: mark_sent uses .to_string() which is a heap allocation side effect inside what should be a pure core function.
findings.failure_mode: The function mutates and allocates rather than being a pure, deterministic calculation. This makes it harder to reason about and benchmark.
findings.fix: If mark_sent is a pure calculation, accept and return domain types (enum-based, no String). Push allocation to the imperative shell layer at I/O boundaries.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent performance or PacketWorkflow allocation patterns
no profiler data for heap allocation hotspots in the packet workflow path
no allocation audit showing try_reserve usage for bounded Vec growth (none present, but no evidence either way)
no command evidence: cargo fmt, cargo test, or cargo clippy were not run
no second-ring analysis (Miri, Kani, or property tests) for state-transition invariants
no command evidence or CLI tooling to validate domain invariants at the boundary
residual_risk: The crate has fundamental architectural violations: status as String, boolean lifecycle flags, no typestates, no Result error type, and no domain newtypes. These are not surface-level issues but core design flaws that make illegal states representable by construction. Static review only; no commands were run to validate findings. The crate would need a full type-level redesign to approach Holzman compliance.
